item.title: Fast \(\ell_\infty\)-Reduction of Rank-2 Lattices in $\mathbb{R}^n$ via a New Reduced-Basis Notion
item.description: arXiv:2610.24719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The shortest vector problem (SVP) under the infinity norm ($\ell_\infty$-norm) is an important lattice problem with applications in lattice-based cryptography. In particular, the security analysis of the post-quantum signature standard ML-DSA highlights the importance of finding short solutions satisfying infinity-norm constraints, rather than only Euclidean norm bounds. However, most existing lattice reduction algorithms are developed for the Euclidean norm, while dedicated studies under the infinity norm remain limited. In this work, we focus on rank-two lattices in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and introduce a new notion of reduced basis under the infinity norm. Based on this definition, we propose an efficient lattice basis reduction algorithm that performs a multi-dimensional analogue of Euclidean division using a dominant coordinate of the basis vectors. Each non-terminal iteration guarantees a factor-two decrease of the maximum infinity norm of the basis vectors. We prove that the algorithm terminates and achieves a bit complexity of $O(nT^2)$, matching the asymptotic complexity order of the classical Lagrange--Gauss reduction. Moreover, the proposed algorithm saves at least $2n$ multiplications per iteration compared with the classical approach. Experiments demonstrate significant runtime improvements, especially for high-dimensional lattices. This work provides a foundation for developing lattice reduction techniques under the infinity norm.
item.dc:creator: Bo Pang, Shaojing Zhang, Chengliang Tian

item.title: Avoiding Distances
item.description: arXiv:2610.24803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a finite planar point set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, let $a_1<a_2< \cdots < a_s$ denote the $s \leq {n \choose 2}$ different (Euclidean) distances between points in $X$. The aim is to retain as many of the points as possible such that certain imposed inter-pair distances are avoided. For example, we show that: (A) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, an independent set of size $0.2293 n$ in the unit distance graph determined by $X$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. For any fixed $k \in \mathbf{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that for any set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, and set $D$ of size $k$, there exists a subset $X' \subseteq X$ of size $|X'| \geq c_k |X|$ in which no pair of points is at some distance in $D$ (we say that $X'$ avoids distances in $D$). Such a set can be found efficiently. (B) (i) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/2$ that avoids the maximum distance; this bound cannot be improved. (ii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $8n/47$ that avoids both the minimum and maximum distance; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $5n/16$ points can be retained with this property. (iii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/7$ whose diameter is at most half the original diameter; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $n/6$ points can be retained with this property. (C) (i) For any $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for \textsc{MIS} in the minimum distance graph of $n$ points in the plane can be found in $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)} n^{O(1)}$ time. (ii) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, a maximum independent set in the graph of diameters can be computed in $O(n^2)$ time. The techniques used to handle the planar case can be extended to $\mathbf{R}^d$ for any fixed dimension $d$.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Dumitrescu, Zsolt L\'angi

item.title: Union of Translates of a Convex Body
item.description: arXiv:2610.25841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of calculating the volume of the union of translates of a strictly convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. When $K$ is a ball, it is possible to simplify the inclusion-exclusion formula by summing over only a small subset of all terms. This subset corresponds to intersecting cells in the Voronoi diagram of the ball centers. We prove that the same simplification is valid for every strictly convex $K$ if and only if $d\leq 2$. Moreover, in three dimensions and when $K$ is $C^4$, we use the Fubini-Pick affine invariant to show that the topological identity underlying this technique holds if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid.
item.dc:creator: Alec Shelley, Daniel Tartakovsky

item.title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.23920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For integers $r \ge 3$, $c \ge 2$, and $s \ge 0$, let $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ denote the smallest integer such that any set of at least $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ points in the plane in general position (no three on a line), colored with $c$ colors, contains a monochromatic $r$-gon (not necessarily convex) with at most $s$ interior points. Define $\lambda_r^{\star}(c)$ to be the smallest integer such that $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,\lambda_r^{\star}(c)) < \infty$. The case of triangles, that is, $r=3$, has been studied in recent years. In this paper, we establish bounds on $\lambda_r^{\star}(c)$, for $r \ge 4$. Specifically, in the bichromatic case, we prove that $\lambda_r^{\star}(2)\leq \lfloor\frac{r-2}{2}\rfloor$, for every $r\geq3$. For hexagons, we sharpen this bound to $\lambda_6^{\star}(2)\leq1$, that is, every sufficiently large bichromatic planar point set in general position contains a monochromatic hexagon with at most one interior point. Next, for any number of colors $c\geq3$ and $r\geq3$, we show that $$(r - 2) \left \lfloor \frac{c-1}{2} \right \rfloor \leq \lambda_r^\star(c) \leq (r-2)(c-2)+\left\lfloor(r-2)\delta_c\right\rfloor, $$ for some constant $\delta_c \in (0, \frac{1}{2}]$, depending on $c$. The upper bounds combine spiral polygonizations with nested convex-hull arguments and, in the hexagon case, incidence counting in $4$-connected triangulations. The lower bounds follow from colored Horton-set constructions.
item.dc:creator: Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya, Sandip Das, Sk Samim Islam, Aashirwad Mohapatra, Saumya Sen

item.title: Dimension Thresholds for Relative-Error Representations of Finite Metrics in Pseudo-Euclidean Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A finite metric space with $N$ points admits an exact representation in a pseudo-Euclidean space of dimension at most $N-1$. We study the minimum dimension required for relative-error approximation of squared distances. Our main result gives an upper bound for arbitrary metrics in terms of local distance ratios: for $4/5<\varepsilon<1$, dimension $O((N/k)\log N+k\rho_k^4\log N/(\varepsilon-4/5)^2)$ suffices, where $\rho_k$ is the largest ratio, over all points, between the distance to the $k$th closest point (counting the point itself) and the nearest-neighbour distance. The proof combines a low-rank landmark approximation with a sparse correction controlled by its factorization norm. For metrics with distances in $[1,\Phi]$, where $\Phi\ge5$ is fixed, the worst-case dimension is $\Theta(N)$ for $0<\varepsilon<4/5$, lies between $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ and $O(\sqrt N\log N)$ for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, and is $\Theta(\log N)$ for $\varepsilon>(\Phi^2-1)/(\Phi^2+1)$. For $\Phi>5$, an intermediate range remains without matching bounds. Sign-pattern counting yields the $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ lower bound for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, while Hadamard matrices give explicit linear lower bounds for $\varepsilon<4/5$ via a known approximate-rank estimate. We also construct configurations with null squared intervals whose minimum representation dimension remains $N-1$ for every $\varepsilon<1$. Finally, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<3/5$, we show that the quadratic dependence on the parameter $C$ in the dimension bound derived from Deng et al.'s pseudo-Euclidean Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is necessary up to a logarithmic factor.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Muravya, Aleksandr Bespalov, Anna Vozianova

item.title: Near-Linear Time Maximum Clique in Circular Arc Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.24339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a near-linear time algorithm to find a maximum clique in circular arc graphs, the intersection graphs of arcs on the circumference of a circle, answering a 30-year-old open question posed by Bhattacharya and Kaller [J. Algorithms 1997] and Tiskin [CPM 2006]. Our algorithm runs in time $O(n\log^2 n)$, given $n$ circular arcs, where the graph is implicit. Previous approaches take at least quadratic time (unless the implicitly given graph is sparse). To overcome the quadratic barrier, we solve (structured and related) instances of bipartite matching by interpreting them as a single, offline 2D dominance problem, which in turn we model as a shortest paths problem in a planar grid graph. This allows for the final step, which builds on the theory of Monge matrices to obtain sparse representation and efficient distance computations in the grid graph. Additionally, we provide an observation about the structure of circular arc cliques that leads to an algorithm for the weighted version of the problem with a new parameter, the minimum load $d$, which we define as the minimum, over all points on the circle, of the number of arcs containing that point. The algorithm runs in time $O(dn\log\log n + n\log n)$. This is always at least as good as the previous best maximum weight clique algorithm, which runs in time $O(m\log\log n + n\log n)$, where $m$ denotes the number of edges in the implicit intersection graph, because the minimum load satisfies $d \le 2m/n$. [Abstract shortened to meet arXiv's requirements.]
item.dc:creator: Dario Moschetti, Adam Polak, Jonas Schmidt

item.title: Navigable Graphs for Low-Dimensional Hyperbolic Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A directed graph on a point set $P$ in a metric space $(X,d)$ is navigable if for every ordered pair of distinct points $s,t \in P$, $s$ has an out-neighbor $v$ with $d(v,t) < d(s,t)$, so greedy routing always reaches the destination. Existing work on sparse navigable graphs mostly assumes bounded doubling dimensions. In this paper, we show that constant-dimensional hyperbolic spaces that do not have bounded doubling dimension also admit sparse navigable graphs. Specifically, for an $n$-point set in $\mathbb H^k$ with a constant $k$, we construct a navigable graph of size $O_k(n)$ with Steiner points, where each node has constant out-degree. We also show that Steiner points can be removed: every $n$-point set in $\mathbb H^k$ admits a navigable graph on the input points alone with $O_k(n)$ edges, though a single vertex may have out-degree $\Omega(n)$. Furthermore, with a refined construction with $O_k(n\log n)$ edges and an accompanying greedy routing algorithm, we can obtain routing paths of expected $O(\log ^2 n)$ in both settings with or without Steiner points. With Steiner points, the maximum out-degree is bounded by $O_k(\log n)$. We complement these upper bounds with matching lower bound results. In the hyperbolic plane, there are point sets for which every navigable graph requires maximum out-degree $\Omega(n)$, so the maximum linear out-degree above is unavoidable and constant out-degree is only possible with Steiner points. Next, we show that for every constant $\alpha>1$, an $\alpha$-navigable graph may require $\Omega(n^2)$ edges, which rules out the standard route of using $\alpha$-navigability to obtain greedy paths of bounded hops. Last, once the dimension $k$ reaches $\Omega(\log n)$, there are point sets for which every navigable graph may require $n^{3/2-o(1)}$ edges, matching the upper bounds for general metrics.
item.dc:creator: Chengyuan Deng, Jie Gao, Kuijun Liu, Kevin Lu, Feng Luo, Puheng Weng, Cheng Xin

item.title: A Strongly-Subquadratic $(3+\varepsilon)$-Approximation for the Fr\'echet Distance for Paths in Metric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.08893v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Fr\'echet distance is a well-studied distance measure for paths in a metric space. It is mostly studied for paths in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Here, computing the Fr\'echet distance between two polylines takes time roughly quadratic in the number of vertices. Assuming the strong exponential time hypothesis (SETH), it cannot be approximated to within a factor less than $3$ in strongly-subquadratic time. Recently, it was shown that for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a randomized algorithm that can compute a $(7+\varepsilon)$-approximation in strongly-subquadratic expected time [Cheng, Huang, and Zhang; STOC'25]. For polylines with $n$ and $m$ vertices in a Euclidean space of constant dimension, where $n \geq m$, their algorithm takes $O(nm^{0.99} \log(n/\varepsilon))$ time in expectation. We present a deterministic approximation algorithm that significantly improves upon the approximation factor and running time. Specifically, our algorithm computes a $(3+\varepsilon)$-approximation in $O(nm^{2/3} \log n \cdot \log (\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \log n))$ time. Our algorithm nearly matches the conditional lower bound on the approximation factor implied by SETH. For polylines in $\mathbb{R}$, we present a $3$-approximation algorithm that runs in $O(nm^{2/3} \log^{5/3} n)$ time, and exactly matches the conditional lower bound. For our results, we introduce a general strongly-subquadratic time $3$-approximate decision algorithm. This algorithm makes no assumptions on the ambient metric space, and relies only on standard assumptions on the so-called free space of the input paths. Under some mild assumptions, our decision algorithm leads to a $(3+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm in general metric spaces. These assumptions hold automatically for polylines in any metric space $(\mathbb{R}^d, L_p)$ with $p \geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Thijs van der Horst, Tim Ophelders

item.title: Geometric $(1+\varepsilon)$-Spanners with Few Crossings
item.description: arXiv:2607.25040v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $n$ points in the plane and $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(n/\varepsilon)$ edges in which every edge has $\tilde{O}(1/\varepsilon^3)$ crossings, the total number of crossings is $\tilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^4)$, and the ratio between the lengths of any two crossing edges is $O(1/\varepsilon^2)$. Our spanner construction substantially improves on the previous upper bound for the number of crossings in a $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner, and it is the first spanner construction that ensures $O(1)$ crossings per edge for any constant $\varepsilon>0$. In contrast, we construct $n$ points in the plane for which every $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner has $\Omega(n/\varepsilon^3)$ crossings, $n$ points for which every $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner has an edge with $\Omega(1/\varepsilon^{5/2})$ crossings, and 4 points for which every $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner contains two crossing edges where one is $\Omega(1/\varepsilon)$ times longer than the other.
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luu, Csaba D. T\'oth

item.title: The Stretch Factor of Planar Delaunay Triangulations Is Less Than 1.5949
item.description: arXiv:2609.07979v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stretch factor of a triangulation is the maximum, over all pairs of its vertices, of the ratio between their shortest-path distance in the triangulation and their Euclidean distance. Determining the worst-case stretch factor of planar Delaunay triangulations is a long-standing open problem in computational geometry; the best known lower and upper bounds have been 1.5932, due to Xia and Zhang, and 1.998, due to Xia. Xia's induction over the circumdisks of the triangles crossed by the segment between two vertices compares shortest paths along their circles with polylines whose lengths do not split into contributions of single disks, so it has to be completed by a global estimate that loses a constant factor. In this paper, we propose progress accounting: the chords shared by consecutive circumdisks cut the segment into parts, one for each disk, and we call the length of the part of a disk its progress; the progresses add up exactly to the length of the segment. The length of a shortest path along the circles also splits into local terms, one for each disk, which are computed from the shortest distances to the two ends of each shared chord; an upper bound U then follows from a potential function whose decrease pays, at every disk, for its term minus U times its progress. We show that such a potential exists whenever a function of four variables satisfies five explicit conditions. We then construct such a function, which satisfies one of the conditions by construction, and verify the other four by a computer-assisted proof in exact rational and interval arithmetic. As a result, every Delaunay triangulation of a finite planar point set has stretch factor at most 79742997/50000000 < 1.59486, which reduces the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds from 0.405 to less than 0.0017.
item.dc:creator: Guanlin Mo, Kangke Cheng, Hu Ding

item.title: The Rhythm of the Tiles: Narrow and Low Temperature Computation and Simulation in Synchronous Tile Self-Assembly
item.description: arXiv:2610.17112v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the synchronicity provided by the syncTAM can be leveraged to perform two additional feats impossible in the asynchronous aTAM. The aTAM has long been known to be equivalent to finite automata in the one-dimensional case. For our first set of results, we prove that this still holds when a finite, fixed amount of space is available in the second dimension. Yet, surprisingly, in the synchronous setting, a small, fixed, width is enough to simulate a Turing Machine. This holds even in the non-cooperative setting. For our second set of main results we prove that there exists a single set of syncTAM tiles that can be used to simulate any syncTAM system simply by using those tiles to create a scaled version of the seed structure of the original system and then letting the tiles from that set self-assemble from the scaled seed structure. While it has been shown (FOCS 2012) that such a tile set also exists in the aTAM for simulating all aTAM systems, that "intrinsically universal" (IU) tile set requires cooperativity (and is impossible without cooperativity as shown in SODA 2014). We prove there exists an IU tile set in the syncTAM that works without cooperativity. Furthermore, there exists a tile set that is IU for the class of directed systems (i.e. systems which each have a single terminal assembly) while remaining directed during simulation. This was shown to be impossible in the aTAM (FOCS 2016).
item.dc:creator: Florent Becker, Phillip Drake, Benjamin Durbin, Nicolas Ollinger, Brent Orlina, Matthew J. Patitz

item.title: OUGS: Active View Selection via Object-aware Uncertainty Estimation in 3DGS
item.description: arXiv:2511.09397v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have achieved state-of-the-art results for novel view synthesis. However, efficiently capturing high-fidelity reconstructions of specific objects within complex scenes remains a significant challenge. A key limitation of existing active reconstruction methods is their reliance on scene-level uncertainty metrics, which are often biased by irrelevant background clutter and lead to inefficient view selection for object-centric tasks. We present OUGS, a novel framework that addresses this challenge with a more principled, physically-grounded uncertainty formulation for 3DGS. Our core innovation is to derive uncertainty directly from the explicit physical parameters of the 3D Gaussian primitives (e.g., position, scale, rotation). By propagating the covariance of these parameters through the rendering Jacobian, we establish a highly interpretable uncertainty model. This foundation allows us to then seamlessly integrate semantic segmentation masks to produce a targeted, object-aware uncertainty score that effectively disentangles the object from its environment. This allows for a more effective active view selection strategy that prioritizes views critical to improving object fidelity. Experimental evaluations on public datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the efficiency of the 3DGS reconstruction process and achieves higher quality for targeted objects compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, while also serving as a robust uncertainty estimator for the global scene.
item.dc:creator: Haiyi Li, Qi Chen, Denis Kalkofen, Hsiang-Ting Chen

item.title: Any 3D Scene is Worth 1K Tokens: 3D-Grounded Representation for Scene Generation at Scale
item.description: arXiv:2604.11331v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. Typically, these 2D-based approaches perform scene generation in a 2D latent space, which introduces two fundamental issues: (i) representing 3D scenes via 2D views leads to significant representation redundancy, and (ii) latent space rooted in 2D inherently limits the spatial consistency of the generated scenes. In this paper, we propose to perform 3D scene generation directly within a high-dimensional implicit 3D latent space derived from powerful 2D foundation models (e.g., DINOv2, SigLIP2, DA3). Then we tame diffusion transformers to perform diffusion modeling directly in the 3D latent space, enabling 3D-grounded scene generation. In our experiments, we not only demonstrate the advantages of our method over 2D-based approaches in terms of efficiency and spatial consistency, but also comprehensively analyze the impact of 3D latent representation on 3D scene generation performance. Furthermore, we validate the favorable scalability of our method with respect to representation and model capacity.
item.dc:creator: Dongxu Wei, Qi Xu, Zhiqi Li, Hangning Zhou, Cong Qiu, Hailong Qin, Mu Yang, Zhaopeng Cui, Peidong Liu
